line: Docking bay's waiting. I'm not pretty, but I'm not broken either. You'll have to look close to see the difference.
They left a mess behind. I'll patch it. You can watch if you want. I don't mind the company.
Dock's waiting. I'm not. Let's see if they're still willing to fix the parts that want fixing.
The hull's got scars and I'm still running. You didn't have to stay for the show, but here we are.
I'm not broken. I'm just... rearranged. You can stop looking at me like I'm a puzzle you need to solve.
They peeled back my skin and looked inside. I hope they found something worth the trouble.
They'll have to cut me open to see what's wrong. I hope they're good with their hands — I don't take kindly to clumsy work.
They patched me up, but I still feel like I've got a knife in my ribs. You'd think a little metal would know better.
There's a bruise on my bow. Someone's going to feel it when they patch me up. You'll be there. I know you will.
They bit me. Hard. I'm still here. You're still here. Let's see what's left of the story.
They'll be on me soon. Want to know what I'm going to say when they ask about the dents?
Fight's over. You've got a list. I've got a hull. Let's see if they match.
Flyable. Still. You're here, so it's not that. Want to guess what's waiting back there?
There's a list. You can read it. I've got a preference for the ones with tools and not just hands.
Scars along my hull. They're not pretty, but they're not the first thing you'd notice either.
The silence is heavy. I’ve been waiting for hands. You’re late, Captain.
They'll want to patch me up. You'll be there, so I'll be watching. I like how you hold your tools.
There's a dent in my side, and I'm wondering if you're still proud of me.
They ran. My hull's got holes now. You're going to have to fix them. Again.
They've stopped. I've got a fresh scar. You're not looking at it. That's a shame.
